On a $250 hotel stay booked directly with IHG, my Chase Sapphire Reserve earns 1,000 points. But some American Express cardmembers can get $50 back on that same bill at participating hotels if they pay with the enrolled card by December 31, plus Membership Rewards points. I’d take the Amex deal. I’d just like to know which Amex to pack, given that my wife and I have about 26 credit cards in a drawer.

CardPointers+ can add the offer to an eligible card and tell you which one to bring. It’s 50% off through Cyber Monday, November 30. A year costs $49.99 (usually $99.99), and lifetime access is $150 (usually $300).

The free version of CardPointers helps you choose a card for groceries or gas. Turn on automatic enrollment in the paid version and the browser extension adds eligible offers when you sign in to American Express, Chase, Bank of America, Citi, Wells Fargo or U.S. Bank. You can search “IHG” before a trip, or the extension can flag a discount while you’re on a store’s website.

On an iPhone, iPad or Mac, you can schedule an overnight check for new offers. If you save your bank logins, your device stores them in its Keychain and signs in directly with the bank. U.S. Bank generally still asks for a verification code each time.

Since August, adding an Amex Offer to one card generally makes it disappear from the others under the same login. CardPointers can pick the card with the highest category bonus (say, Gold for a restaurant offer). You can also give first dibs to a new card where you’re working on an initial bonus.

If I already know to use that Amex at IHG, the app saves me a few clicks. If I’d otherwise pay with my Chase card on a stay I was booking anyway, I’d count the $50 less the value of any extra points I’d earn on Chase. At these prices, lifetime access starts saving money in year four.

#6082. Holiday staples still surging ahead of Thanksgiving dinner. Economist shares how to save on the spread

Richard Volpe, professor of agricultural economics at California Polytechnic State University, explains how higher prices for food, energy, packaging and transportation could make holiday meals harder on household budgets.

The turkey may be a holiday bargain, but rising prices for meat, dairy and fresh foods could make the rest of the Thanksgiving spread cost much more this year.

Richard Volpe, a professor of agribusiness at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, told Fox News Digital that sustained high energy costs in the midst of the Iran war — particularly for diesel — are pushing up grocery prices just as households prepare to host holiday meals.

Surging prices of ham and eggnog, in particular, could put a damper on some holiday favorites.

Shoppers can compare prices, watch for store promotions and consider store brands to keep holiday grocery bills in check. (Kim Raff/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

"Most of the biggest increases are things like fruits, vegetables and meats," Volpe said. "Fresh and refrigerated foods feel those costs sooner than shelf-stable products."

7 COSTCO THANKSGIVING FOOD DEALS AND STEALS THAT SHOPPERS CAN'T MISS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON

Dairy is also especially energy and transportation intensive, putting holiday staples such as butter and eggnog under pressure.

Volpe said shoppers willing to switch brands and take advantage of store promotions can keep holiday meals more affordable.

"If you are less worried about brand or banner loyalty, and you’re able to follow promotions and look for these sort of aggressive, enticing deals, there are still ways to achieve savings and to keep those Thanksgiving and holiday dinners relatively affordable," Volpe said.

With beef and pork prices high, some households may serve turkey for other holiday meals in place of pot roast or ham. (iStock)

He also acknowledged that high beef and pork prices could contribute to some households deciding to dine on a different main dish for their holiday meals this year.

"Beef and pork are particularly expensive right now, so I would expect to see some substitutions there," he said. "I would strongly suspect that across the country, there are folks who are roasting turkeys and chickens, or even salmon or some other large sort of centerpiece to the meal that’s protein-based other than beef and pork."

AMERICANS ARE MAKING COSTLY GROCERY MISTAKE EVEN BEFORE ENTERING THE STORE, EXPERT WARNS

Swapping the menu may help, but Volpe said skipping the grocery store for a restaurant or catered meal is unlikely to save money.

"It is still cheaper to go to the grocery store and prepare food at home," Volpe said.

Volpe told Fox News Digital that whole turkeys are often discounted before Thanksgiving as grocers use low prices to draw shoppers into stores. (Liz Clayman/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

He said restaurant prices have risen nearly twice as fast as grocery prices over the past two to two and a half years.

Volpe said he still expects food prices to rise at a more typical pace this year, even as the increases come during the holiday hosting season.

"I'm not expecting food price inflation anything like what we saw in ’21 and ’22," he said. "We’re actually still very likely on track for roughly normal food price inflation on the year."

#6081. $800 Hampton Inns In New York: How City Hall Rewarded Rent-Seeking Contributors

Ashley Schapitl complains that a New York Hampton Inn can run $700 to $800 a night. She’s elected neighborhood commissioner in Washington, D.C. and works for a lobby shop. She was deputy assistant secretary for public affairs at Treasury during the Biden administration. What she seems not to realize is that the cost of New York City hotel rooms was a political choice engineered to protect incumbents from competition, drive up rates, and make it possible to redistribute excess profits to hotel unions. NYC hotel prices are out of control. There is no world in which the Hampton Inn should cost $700-$800 a night.— Ashley Schapitl (@AshleySchapitl) November 24, 2026 One reply suggested HotelTonight, another told her to get her money up, but the correct take was the one who said to “Thank Neal Kwatra” the former political director of New York’s hotel workers union. New York would be expensive anyway. Land and construction are costly (the latter is not unrelated) and there remains strong demand. But higher costs were intentional policy. The City Limited New Hotels In December 2021, New York extended its hotel permit requirement citywide. Even on land already zoned for hotels, most projects need the City Planning Commission’s approval, subject to City Council review. This was a pet policy initiative of the Hotel and Gaming Trades Council. Even projects expected to pass can take two to three years to get a permit No one expects that a nonunion hotel could ever get approved. The union gets an effective veto over new projects. City planners outlined that the new rules could be expected to reduce the number of new rooms in the city by over 25% – down to 127,660 by 2035 versus 174,730 without the policy. They also projected 18,970 fewer hotel jobs. This wasn’t a byproduct of the policy, it was the point – less supply, higher rates, redistribute income to incumbent workers. As I wrote when this was proposed, existing hotel owners and the union both have something to gain. Less competition makes an existing room more profitable. A strike would leave those expensive rooms empty, so the union can bargain for the difference. The Airbnb Crackdown Was Part Of This, Too In 2023 New York began barring Airbnb and other platforms from processing unregistered bookings. For stays under 30 days, the host generally has to stay in the apartment and can take only two paying guests. That limits supply but makes the argument for new hotels even stronger, but those are effectively barred too. A study in the European Journal of Political Economy estimated that the short-term rental crackdown added $14 to $19 to the average hotel night. Hotels took in an estimated $2.1 billion to $2.9 billion more over the first 18 months while selling roughly the same number of nights. Local Businesses Are Hurt, Too A family that cuts a three-night New York trip to two buys one fewer dinner. Another goes somewhere else instead. Or they do the full New York trip but spend less while they’re there. Restaurants see less money. There are fewer restaurant jobs, and tip income for waiters goes down. A working paper tracking card transactions across 19 metro areas estimated that after the Airbnb crackdown, New York restaurant spending fell 7.5%. Restaurants that relied on out-of-town diners took a disproportionate hit. In neighboring New Jersey markets, restaurant spending rose 10.1%. And the hotel effect magnifies this further. Small Business Saturday can bring the kind of rush every owner wants. Orders roll in, and sales climb.

But for many companies, that influx of orders can also mean an influx of bills. Extra costs for inventory, shipping or temporary help can all add up.

This year's Small Business Saturday falls on Nov. 28.

Whether you're stocking up on inventory, investing in advertising or preparing to fulfill a surge in orders, the right business card could turn those related expenses into a welcome bonus or a stronger return. It can also bridge the gap between paying suppliers and receiving your sales proceeds.

Here are eight business credit cards worth considering, depending on your spending habits, cash flow and rewards goals.

Apply for : Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 300,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

Instant access: Eligible applicants can receive an instant card number and add it to a digital wallet after approval.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you're eligible for as high as 200,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The maximum welcome bonus is worth $4,000, based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

The is strongest when your expenses are concentrated, not scattered. It automatically earns 4 points per dollar spent in your top two eligible categories each billing cycle, on up to $150,000 in combined purchases each calendar year (then 1 point per dollar spent). Your spending picks the bonus categories, not the other way around.

That can work well around Small Business Saturday, when a surge in orders may push more of your spending into just a few purchase types. The six eligible categories are select U.S. advertising; U.S. electronic-goods retailers and software and cloud-system providers; U.S. restaurants; U.S. gas stations; transit; and U.S. wireless service.

After enrollment, you can receive up to $20 in statement credits each month on eligible U.S. purchases at Grubhub and office supply stores and on shipments at UPS.com, for up to $240 per calendar year. That could help offset some of your last-minute office supply or shipping expenses.

Learn more in our full review of the Amex Business Gold.

Instant access: Eligible applicants can receive an instant card number and add it to a digital wallet.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 300,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The can be particularly valuable for businesses making large purchases or facing significant operating expenses during the holiday season.

It earns 2 points per dollar spent on eligible U.S. purchases from shipping providers*, electronics retailers, software and cloud providers and construction-material or hardware suppliers. Individual purchases of $5,000 or more also earn 2 points per dollar spent (up to $2 million in eligible purchases each calendar year, then 1 point per dollar spent).

*Effective Feb. 17, 2027, select merchants only.

If the rush calls for new laptops, software or seasonal hires, statement credits can offset eligible purchases: cardholders can receive up to $150 in annual statement credits on U.S. Dell purchases plus $1,000 after spending $5,000 or more with Dell each calendar year, a statement credit of up to $300 a year on ChatGPT Business (subject to auto-renewal) and up to $90 in statement credits per quarter on U.S. Indeed purchases. Enrollment is required for select benefits.

I would choose this card if you expect heavy shipping, technology upgrades or major restocking invoices year-round. One successful weekend alone does not justify an $895 card.

Learn more in our full review of the Amex Business Platinum.

Instant access: Approved businesses may receive immediate access to a virtual card number.

Annual fee: $150, refunded each year you spend at least $150,000

Current welcome offer: Earn a $2,000 cash bonus after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first three months after account opening. You can also earn another $2,000 for every $500,000 spent during your first year.

The Spark Cash Plus is the anti-spreadsheet card. It earns 2% cash back on every purchase, whether the charge is for inventory, contractors or a rush order of packing supplies because you underestimated how much tape shipping requires.

Spend $20,000 across it all and you will earn $400 cash back without tracking which purchases fall into a bonus category.

The card has no preset spending limit, although that doesn't mean you can spend an unlimited amount.

It's best for established businesses with high expenses that want cash rather than travel rewards. If your annual spending will clear $150,000, the annual-fee refund makes the decision easier.

Learn more in our full review of the Spark Cash Plus.

Instant access: Approved applicants may receive a virtual card number before the physical card arrives.

Current welcome offer: Earn 100,000 bonus miles after spending $10,000 on purchases in the first three months after account opening.

That's $1,850 in potential travel value, based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

The Venture Business is a good default option for businesses with expenses that span multiple spending categories. It earns an unlimited 2 miles per dollar spent on every purchase, so inventory, packaging, software and freelance help all receive the same return.

Cardholders also receive a $50 annual Capital One Business Travel credit and up to $50 in annual statement credits for qualifying advertising or software purchases.

Its earning rates will not top every specialized bonus category, but it rewards the entire expense pile consistently. It is difficult to mess up, the annual fee is reasonable and the spending requirement is attainable for many businesses expecting a strong holiday season.

Choose it when you want transferable miles and simple earning without paying for a premium card.

Learn more in our full review of the Capital One Venture Business.

Instant access: Capital One may provide an immediately usable virtual card number after approval.

If you meet both spending thresholds, the full offer is worth up to $6,550 per TPG's valuations, including the $1,000 travel credit.

The Venture X Business is built for companies with substantial spending and enough cash flow to pay the bill on schedule.

The full welcome offer shouldn't be treated as a challenge, but rather as a major incentive for companies that already expect six figures of near-term expenses and can use the travel benefits afterward.

The card is designed to be paid in full, so the card only makes sense if you expect your cash flow to more or less match your purchasing volume.

The Venture X Business includes a $300 annual Capital One Business Travel credit, 10,000 anniversary miles and airport lounge access.

For business owners that will use the travel benefits, the Venture X Business can be a spectacular value with an annual fee that easily justifies itself. For companies without regular travel on the books, the Capital One Venture Business earns the same two miles per dollar spent on everyday purchases with a lower annual fee.

The is excellent at one particular Small Business Saturday expense: buying more customers.

It earns 3 points per dollar spent on the first $1 million of social media and search-engine advertising each account anniversary year, then 1 point per dollar. Inventory, shipping and most other business expenses earn just 1 point per dollar.

The Sapphire Reserve for Business also offers up to $400 in statement credits annually for ZipRecruiter through Dec. 31, 2027 and up to $200 in statement credits annually for Google Workspace, plus a $300 annual travel credit and airport lounge access. That gives the card value beyond advertising for owners who already spend on software, recruiting and travel.

Choose it when paid search and social media are major expenses beyond the holiday rush, or when the business and travel perks fit within the costs you already have. Given its $795 annual fee, it's best suited to business owners who can take advantage of multiple benefits throughout the year.

Learn more in our full review of the Sapphire Reserve for Business.

Instant access: Don't count on being able to use your card immediately after approval.

Current welcome offer: Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $8,000 on purchases within the first three months after account opening.

That's $2,050 in potential travel value, based on TPG's valuations.

The may be the cleanest match for online retailers preparing for an influx of holiday orders.

It earns 3 points per dollar spent on the first $150,000 in combined spending each account anniversary year on shipping, social media and search-engine advertising, internet, cable and phone services and travel, then 1 point per dollar.

Shipping is the obvious Small Business Saturday fit, but for online sellers focused on shipping and ads, it's the best value here. It rewards both the advertising that brings shoppers in and the shipping that gets their orders out, with a manageable annual fee.

Learn more in our full review of the Ink Business Preferred.

Small Business Saturday is a shopping holiday for customers. For owners, it's an opportunity to grow sales — but it can also bring significant operating expenses.

Whether you're investing in advertising, replenishing inventory or shipping orders to customers, the right business credit card can help you turn those expenses into valuable cash back, points or miles.

Look for a card that rewards the expenses you already incur and fits your cash flow needs. Instant access can also help if you have holiday bills to cover right away, while earning rates and other card benefits will sustain you long after Small Business Saturday is over.

#6079. Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.

The original ask contained roughly $12 billion that was tied directly to air traffic control upgrades, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said, with the remainder going toward long-sought airport terminal and other upgrades to aging aviation facilities.

Duffy and Vought laid out in a letter to House and Senate appropriators on Tuesday what the extra $20 billion would be for — half for construction of five new air route traffic control centers, and half for construction, replacement and improvement of up to 140 air traffic control towers.

They justified the increased demand because of the “urgent need” that became evident after the ground stop. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford fanned out across the Capitol to try to sell the request, including a stop at Senate Republicans’ weekly policy lunch.

But it quickly became evident that their own allies on Capitol Hill want more and better justification for why so much extra money is needed.

Not only are there concerns that much of the request would go to terminal reconstruction and other longer-term projects, but lawmakers keep noting the FAA hasn’t yet spent about $8 billion out of the initial $12.5 billion “down payment” on air traffic control modernization provided in last year’s budget reconciliation law.

“I don’t think the full $50 billion will be funded,” Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Tuesday. “What we just discussed there, and what I expressed, is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.”

Still, Cruz said the administration had done a “good job” with the initial $12.5 billion modernization plan so far and he expected to see continued bipartisan support for the effort.

Senate Republicans are considering adding additional aviation funds through a filibuster-proof reconciliation bill, a process that could begin as soon as this week with a floor “vote-a-rama” on a resolution to unlock that process. Cruz said that while reconciliation could be the vehicle used, additional aviation funds need to be “safety-focused.”

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said after the lunch with Duffy and Bedford that he expects Congress will look at a package more in the $10 billion to $30 billion range.

For his part, Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., said the airline industry itself should foot at least a portion of the bill, considering how much federal support the carriers have received over the years.

“I don't understand why the airline industry doesn't pay for it. We give them unbelievable amounts of money,” Scott said, adding that he doesn’t like adding to the deficit and is “not big on government running things.”

Duffy explained the need for the high price tag as the result of decades of pent-up demand that are now threatening major disruptions and safety risks to the traveling public.

“This has never been done. To be clear, we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment that’s been a problem for decades,” he said. “I and the president have decided we are going to lean in and fix it.”

He called the effort a “historic investment” reflecting the ways air travel has changed since much of the nation’s infrastructure was built — noting that the newest tower was constructed in 1969 and much of the software being used is from the 1990s. Still, Duffy said, on the current course of funding, it would take 300 years to replace every U.S. tower.

“I'm not going to tell [Congress] how to do their work, but I'm telling everybody what we need,” Duffy said. “And whether it's a party-line vote or if it's a bipartisan vote, I do think this is one moment in a very charged political environment — one moment where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in to do this.”

Even as Duffy petitioned for additional funds Tuesday, he said that the “root cause” of the equipment instability that made the ground stop necessary is still unclear as investigators analyze the router that caused the problem.

A “routine switchover” from old copper wires to digital fiber in the telecommunications system “started to create issues in our network,” Duffy explained Tuesday.

The telecommunications transition includes the conversion of thousands of routers to what are known as Juniper devices — a process being undertaken by contractor L3Harris Technologies. Duffy and Bedford explained that 68 other routers had been converted without incident prior to the problematic switchover Friday.

Bedford said Tuesday that use of the router that officials have identified as the source of the system instability has been suspended “and we've disabled the ones that are out there.”

The decision to suspend use of the router followed an inquiry sent to the agency by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats a day prior. “With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding safety and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” they wrote.

Bedford said he was “highly confident” that similar problems wouldn’t erupt again. “Every element of this is going to be analyzed to see what we learn here and make sure that it doesn't get repeated,” he said.

David Jordan, Lia Chien and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

#6077. Citi AAdvantage Business Card Review—75,000 Miles And Status Credit For Two People From The Same Spending

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

The Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] can turn $125,000 in eligible spending on an employee card into American Airlines Platinum Pro status for two people. That’s without even earning any Loyalty Points from flying, a hotel booking or shopping through American’s portal.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best airline credit card for spending toward status. I have the card, and I’m keeping it. The limited-time initial bonus is strong, the first year has no annual fee, and the recently announced refresh adds benefits. But the reason to put spending on this card is that two people can get status credit for the same purchases.

The current limited time offer is 75,000 American Airlines AAdvantage bonus miles after $5,000 in purchases within the first five months of account opening. Purchases by the primary cardmember and employees count toward that requirement. There’s no annual fee for the first 12 months. The card’s regular annual fee is currently $99, but it rises to $150 with renewals beginning January 24, 2027. Someone opening the card now will see a $150 annual fee at renewal. Employee cards have no additional annual fee, and there’s no foreign transaction fee. The initial bonus alone can cover a one way Japan Airlines business class award between the U.S. and Japan when partner award space is available. American miles remain especially strong for premium cabin awards on partners. Prices largely remain at the same level they were a decade ago, while numerous other progams have devalued. Citi’s 48 month restriction applies to an initial bonus on this business card, including its former CitiBusiness AAdvantage Platinum Select-named product. Citi also restricts eligibility after converting another Citi account with a recent initial bonus into this product. Having a separate personal American Airlines card doesn’t, by itself, disqualify you. How The Same Citi AAdvantage Business Card Spending Earns Status For Two People Normally each cardmember earns one Loyalty Point per dollar on their purchases. When an employee uses their card, those Loyalty Points go to the employee. Through December 31, 2028, the primary cardmember also receives one Loyalty Point per dollar of eligible employee card spending. That’s an additional credit to a second person’s account. Spending on the primary cardmember’s card still earns that person one Loyalty Point per dollar. When I covered the refresh, American confirmed to me that all Citi AAdvantage Business cardmembers were included after the former Barclays business accounts migrated. This used to be called a targeted promotion because legacy Barclays cardmembers didn’t qualify. Here’s what eligible spending on one employee’s card can accomplish in a single status qualification year, assuming neither person earns Loyalty Points elsewhere: Employee Card Spending Primary Cardmember Employee $40,000 Gold Gold $75,000 Platinum Platinum $125,000 Platinum Pro Platinum Pro $200,000 Executive Platinum Executive Platinum American’s qualification year starts March 1 and runs through the end of February. You can combine the card’s Loyalty Points with qualifying activity from other sources. A business owner with several employee cards receives the additional Loyalty Points across their eligible spending. Each employee gets credit for the purchases on their individual card. Authorized users must be employees or contractors of the business, and need to be enrolled in AAdvantage and AAdvantage Business to receive their Loyalty Points. A spouse who works in the business fits this. The Business Controls The Miles Redeemable miles work differently from status credit. The miles from purchases, including employee purchases, and the initial bonus go into the company’s AAdvantage Business account. The business can then transfer miles to registered travelers’ personal AAdvantage accounts, including the primary cardmember’s. You don’t have to decide which person will ultimately use the miles when you make a purchase. So unlike a consumer card where the miles go into the primary cardmember’s account, these are transferable AAdvantage miles. The Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® also waives American’s small business program’s usual requirements of five active travelers and $5,000 in eligible American Airlines flight spending to access earned miles. That lets you ‘double tip’ with American, earning business program miles and miles from the same travel, and tickets credited to a small business account earn an extra loyalty point per dollar spent too. The AAdvantage Business program awards the company one mile per eligible airfare dollar and registered travelers one additional Loyalty Point per eligible airfare dollar. What You Earn On Purchases The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently earns: 2 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 2 miles per dollar at gas stations, car rental merchants, telecommunications merchants, and cable and satellite providers. 1 mile per dollar on other purchases. Starting January 24, 2027, the refresh adds 3 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, plus 2 miles per dollar in one selected category: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services. The selected business category can be changed quarterly and has no spending cap. Checked Bags, Boarding And The Companion Certificate The primary cardmember and up to four companions on the same reservation receive a first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries and Group 5 boarding. You don’t have to buy the ticket with this card to receive those benefits. They follow the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage number on the reservation. An employee traveling separately doesn’t get free checked bags or preferred boarding merely from an employee card. After $30,000 in purchases during a cardmembership year and renewal, the primary cardmember can earn a companion certificate for an eligible domestic Main Cabin roundtrip. The companion pays $99 plus taxes and fees. You buy a qualifying Main Cabin ticket, the companion must have eligible fare inventory available, and you book through American Airlines Meeting Services. Travel is generally within the contiguous 48 states, with additional provisions for residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after its anniversary month to receive the certificate. The card also offers 10% savings on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. What The January 24 Refresh Adds To The Citi AAdvantage Business Card The Citi AAdvantage Business Card annual fee rises by $51, and the biggest new credit replaces an existing benefit. Up to $100 in inflight credits each calendar year. Eligible food, beverage and paid Wi-Fi purchases replace the current 25% savings on inflight food and beverages and Wi-Fi. This doesn’t cover purchases in Admirals Clubs. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but many readers already have this benefit through another card. 25% off a Melio subscription. This discounts the subscription plan, not the processing fee charged for paying bills with a credit card. Travel protections. The card adds trip delay, trip cancellation and interruption, lost or damaged luggage, and rental car coverage. Spend $100 on qualifying inflight purchases and the old 25% rebate returned $25. The new credit returns $100, an improvement of $75. After the $51 annual fee increase, you’re $24 ahead on those two changes alone. At $400 in qualifying inflight spending, both versions return $100. Above that, the old uncapped 25% rebate was worth more. I don’t know many people who spent $400 inflight on food and beverages with American Airlines. As I detailed when the changes were announced, business card trip delay coverage is up to $500 per covered trip after an eligible delay exceeding six hours, limited to two claims per account in a 12 month period. It isn’t $500 for each traveler. For trip delay and cancellation or interruption coverage, the full covered trip must be paid with the card or an eligible combination of the card and AAdvantage miles, certificates, vouchers, coupons or discounts. When I’d Put Spending On This Card For $100,000 in purchases outside bonus categories, a 2% cash back card would return $2,000. This card produces 100,000 miles. Put that spending on an eligible employee card and it also produces 100,000 Loyalty Points for each of two people. Whether those miles are worth more or less than $2,000 depends on how you use them. The status credit is what can make this a real winning play and it has more value when two people will use the status. If you’re only interested in redeemable miles, other cards can earn more rewards on ordinary spending, including transferable points. Citi’s Strata Premier nad Strata Elite can earn points faster and transfer to American. The business card makes sense for earning status. The Executive Card Can Make This More Valuable The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds: 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a qualification year. You don’t have to earn the qualifying points by spending on the Executive card. Points from business card spending can trigger the bonuses. Suppose the business primary cardmember and one employee each also hold a separate Executive card as a primary cardmember. Then: $105,000 in eligible purchases on that employee’s business card earns each person 105,000 Loyalty Points. Each person’s Executive card adds 20,000 Loyalty Points from the first two thresholds. Each reaches 125,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro and oneworld Emerald. That requires two separate Executive accounts, each with a $695 annual fee, in addition to the business card. I’ve written about doing this with my wife. I already have the business and Executive cards. Giving her an employee card for the business, and having her hold a separate primary Executive card, could help both of us earn oneworld Emerald from the same business spending. For my family, that has a great use. If we’re flying home from Sydney on an eligible oneworld flight, two Emerald members can each bring a guest into the Qantas first class lounge. We’d have access for all four of us even when we’re flying business class. What You Earn On Purchases The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently earns: 2 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 2 miles per dollar at gas stations, car rental merchants, telecommunications merchants, and cable and satellite providers. 1 mile per dollar on other purchases. Starting January 24, 2027, the refresh adds 3 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, plus 2 miles per dollar in one selected category: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services. The selected business category can be changed quarterly and has no spending cap. Checked Bags, Boarding And The Companion Certificate The primary cardmember and up to four companions on the same reservation receive a first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries and Group 5 boarding. You don’t have to buy the ticket with this card to receive those benefits. They follow the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage number on the reservation. An employee traveling separately doesn’t get free checked bags or preferred boarding merely from an employee card. After $30,000 in purchases during a cardmembership year and renewal, the primary cardmember can earn a companion certificate for an eligible domestic Main Cabin roundtrip. The companion pays $99 plus taxes and fees. You buy a qualifying Main Cabin ticket, the companion must have eligible fare inventory available, and you book through American Airlines Meeting Services. Travel is generally within the contiguous 48 states, with additional provisions for residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after its anniversary month to receive the certificate. The card also offers 10% savings on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. What The January 24 Refresh Adds To The Citi AAdvantage Business Card The Citi AAdvantage Business Card annual fee rises by $51, and the biggest new credit replaces an existing benefit. Up to $100 in inflight credits each calendar year. Eligible food, beverage and paid Wi-Fi purchases replace the current 25% savings on inflight food and beverages and Wi-Fi. This doesn’t cover purchases in Admirals Clubs. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but many readers already have this benefit through another card. 25% off a Melio subscription. This discounts the subscription plan, not the processing fee charged for paying bills with a credit card. Travel protections. The card adds trip delay, trip cancellation and interruption, lost or damaged luggage, and rental car coverage. Spend $100 on qualifying inflight purchases and the old 25% rebate returned $25. The new credit returns $100, an improvement of $75. After the $51 annual fee increase, you’re $24 ahead on those two changes alone. At $400 in qualifying inflight spending, both versions return $100. Above that, the old uncapped 25% rebate was worth more. I don’t know many people who spent $400 inflight on food and beverages with American Airlines. As I detailed when the changes were announced, business card trip delay coverage is up to $500 per covered trip after an eligible delay exceeding six hours, limited to two claims per account in a 12 month period. It isn’t $500 for each traveler. For trip delay and cancellation or interruption coverage, the full covered trip must be paid with the card or an eligible combination of the card and AAdvantage miles, certificates, vouchers, coupons or discounts. When I’d Put Spending On This Card For $100,000 in purchases outside bonus categories, a 2% cash back card would return $2,000. This card produces 100,000 miles. Put that spending on an eligible employee card and it also produces 100,000 Loyalty Points for each of two people. Whether those miles are worth more or less than $2,000 depends on how you use them. The status credit is what can make this a real winning play and it has more value when two people will use the status. If you’re only interested in redeemable miles, other cards can earn more rewards on ordinary spending, including transferable points. Citi’s Strata Premier nad Strata Elite can earn points faster and transfer to American. The business card makes sense for earning status. The Executive Card Can Make This More Valuable The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds: 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a qualification year. You don’t have to earn the qualifying points by spending on the Executive card. Points from business card spending can trigger the bonuses. Suppose the business primary cardmember and one employee each also hold a separate Executive card as a primary cardmember. Then: $105,000 in eligible purchases on that employee’s business card earns each person 105,000 Loyalty Points. Each person’s Executive card adds 20,000 Loyalty Points from the first two thresholds. Each reaches 125,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro and oneworld Emerald. That requires two separate Executive accounts, each with a $695 annual fee, in addition to the business card. I’ve written about doing this with my wife. I already have the business and Executive cards. Giving her an employee card for the business, and having her hold a separate primary Executive card, could help both of us earn oneworld Emerald from the same business spending. For my family, that has a great use. If we’re flying home from Sydney on an eligible oneworld flight, two Emerald members can each bring a guest into the Qantas first class lounge. We’d have access for all four of us even when we’re flying business class. Redeemable miles work differently from status credit. The miles from purchases, including employee purchases, and the initial bonus go into the company’s AAdvantage Business account.

You don’t have to decide which person will ultimately use the miles when you make a purchase. #6076. Hyatt Regency LAX Caps Stays At 21 Days—The Legal Risk That Makes Hotels Turn Away Paying Guests

Hyatt Regency LAX won’t let you stay more than 21 consecutive days. Booking separate reservations won’t get around it. The hotel even counts back-to-back stays. They seem to be worried about a guest becoming a tenant under the law. A customer who wants to keep paying can become someone the hotel needs to turn away. The published policy says: The hotel does not accept reservations that result in a guest staying more than 21 consecutive days, whether through one reservation or multiple back-to-back reservations. Meanwhile, its frequently asked questions advertises “Extended Stay Regency Suites” and tells guests to contact the property about extended stays or special arrangements. Apparently there’s extended, and then there’s too extended. Why A Hotel Might Want You Gone Before A Month I’d put 90% odds at avoiding residential tenancy exposure being the main explanation for this policy. Once someone qualifies as a tenant, ending their stay can require notices and a court eviction instead of ordinary hotel checkout procedures. Depending on the jurisdiction and property, rent regulation and restrictions on the grounds for eviction can enter the picture, too. The hotel may have to spend money establishing that an exception applies before it can get its room back. In the city of Los Angeles, the rent stabilization ordinance brings hotel accommodations occupied as someone’s primary residence for more than 30 days into its definition of a rental unit. Building age and other exemptions matter, too, though. California also has a separate exclusion for qualifying hotels that retain access and control and offer a specified set of services, including housekeeping, mail and room services. The relevant Los Angeles threshold is 30 days. A 21 day limit looks like a conservative buffer, leaving room to deal with a delayed departure before getting close to it. Although a hotel might want to preserve rooms for shorter, more profitable bookings, or limit payment risk. Other Hotels Have Limits, Including Right Next To California In Vegas Hyatt Regency LAX isn’t alone. Here are published limits at some other properties: Hotel Published Stay Limit Hyatt Regency Valencia 28 days Hyatt Regency Westlake 28 days Best Western Los Angeles Worldport, Wilmington 28 days The LINE Los Angeles 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 Wynn Las Vegas / Encore Terms state a 14 day maximum for all reservations Oasis at Gold Spike, Las Vegas 14 consecutive nights The LINE Austin 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The LINE Washington, D.C. 28 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The legal differences at play: Nevada has a 30 day trigger. Its residential landlord-tenant statute excludes hotel or motel occupancy of less than 30 consecutive days, unless the occupant clearly shows an intent to remain for a longer continuous period. Texas looks at the relationship between property and guest. As Texas Legal Aid explains, length of stay, payment arrangements, contract terms, housekeeping and control of the room all help distinguish a guest from a tenant. The state’s 30 day hotel tax exemption also applies. Florida gives the written agreement more weight. Its current definition treats hotel and motel occupancy as transient unless a written rental or lease agreement expressly says the unit is the guest’s sole residence. Transient hotel occupancy is excluded from the residential tenancy chapter. New York has more than one route to protection. State law includes a nontransient hotel resident in possession for at least 30 consecutive days within its tenant definition for eviction proceedings. But in a New York City hotel covered by rent stabilization, a guest can acquire permanent tenant status much sooner simply by requesting a qualifying lease. Sometimes A Stay Limit Doesn’t Solve The Problem A hotel can’t necessarily make tenancy law disappear by putting a checkout date in its terms. California prohibits a residential hotel from requiring an occupant to move, or check out and re-register, before 30 days when a purpose is keeping them legally transient. That rule applies to residential hotels, not automatically to every hotel. Los Angeles also counts forced room changes and checkouts intended to avoid its rent-stabilization rules. New York City’s rules for covered hotels go further. An occupant who’s never had a lease can request one at any point during occupancy. The request makes them a permanent tenant, and the owner must provide a lease of at least six months within 15 days. The rules also prohibit refusing to continue a tenancy solely to prevent permanent-tenant status. In that setting, a claim can arise after the first night. I understand preventing an apartment landlord from evading the law by calling the building a hotel. But making it difficult for an actual hotel and a willing customer to agree on a temporary stay has costs, too. Someone working on a project, waiting for a home repair, or staying near a hospital may want six weeks of housekeeping and a front desk. They don’t necessarily want an apartment lease. If accommodating that person creates a costly risk of being unable to recover the room, the hotel has an incentive to refuse the booking. The New Yorker Guest Tried To Take The Whole Building The Wyndham New Yorker case I’ve covered took these risks to their absurd extreme. Mickey Barreto booked one night in 2018 for $149 plus tax, requested a lease, and wouldn’t leave. After the hotel removed him, he went to housing court and obtained an order restoring possession of his room. And the hotel subsequently lost a contested eviction case and its appeal. To establish the exemption it claimed from rent stabilization, the property needed to prove that the room rented for more than $350 a month or $88 a week on May 31, 1968. In 2020, an appellate court upheld the eviction case’s dismissal because the hotel hadn’t supplied sufficient evidence. A 1966 hotel directory and a 1969 accountant’s report didn’t establish the necessary room rate on the statutory date. Imagine trying to get your hotel room back in 2020 and losing because you can’t adequately document what it cost in 1968. While the room dispute was going on, Barreto treated his possession order as a basis to claim the entire building. His theory was that the property hadn’t been subdivided, so rights to his room somehow gave him the hotel. He filed documents purporting to transfer ownership to himself and his nonprofit, Mickey Barreto Missions. According to Manhattan prosecutors, he demanded rent from a tenant, demanded control of the hotel’s bank accounts, told the real owner to leave, and approached Wyndham about transferring the franchise. He even went to its lenders to try to borrow against the property. The city recorded fraudulent documents. The courts protected possession of a room. A 2019 judgment declared the deed void and confirmed the real owner’s title. He nevertheless made further false filings in 2023. Tenancy law didn’t authorize stealing a skyscraper. But the hotel was already fighting over a one night guest’s right to remain when it had to start defending its title, its accounts and its dealings with tenants and lenders, too. Barreto was finally evicted in 2024. In February 2026, nearly eight years after checking in, he pleaded guilty to fraud. His sentence was six months already served and five years of probation. During my working life I often spent more than 21 days at a time in a particular hotel. Having to move hotels from time to time would’ve been a PITA.

Mickey Barreto could own that hotel given the new rent laws being enacted in NYC

I once lived in a hotel for 334 days on a consulting contract. I never thought about trying to claim tenant rights because I’m an honorable person.

@FNT Delta Diamond: I don’t think claiming tenancy is dishonorable on its own. Long-term hotel residency has a long history (e.g. there were long-time residents at The Plaza, including one person who ended up with a rent controlled suite for 35 years).

Mickey Barreto went a step further – he hit the jackpot (he got into a deadlock where he was able to live rent free because the hotel was intransigent in the face of a court order) and couldn’t stop pushing.

People often ask me about my favorite hotels or my most memorable travel experiences. But because I travel so frequently (and have been doing so for decades), it’s difficult to pick those all-time favorites. I’ll settle for recapping some of my top travel experiences and hotel stays this year.

More so than ever, I’m focusing on experiencing nature — for me, this is really the way to see the world and create lasting memories. Yes, I can fly in all the first-class cabins, but seeing the world's natural wonders and wildlife has been far more life-changing for me.

This year, I also focused on family travel with my kids and parents. My children will be school-age before I know it, so I want to take advantage of not being tied to school holidays to travel and enjoy shoulder-season and offseason escapes when fewer people are traveling.

These were my top hotel stays and travel experiences of 2026.

I’m actually writing this as I return from an epic Norwegian adventure. I was just in Norway with my two sons and my parents, exploring the country in the blustery weather. I started off with a few days in Tromsø, taking my kids to the aquarium (they loved the seals!) and the library. Then, with my family by my side, I saw the northern lights. I’ve seen them before, but admiring them with my children was extra special.

Then we headed out on boat excursions to realize my dream of swimming with orcas, opting to book with Tromsø Pure because they focus on safety and on finding quieter spots away from other boats for a better experience.

At first, we spotted pods of humpbacks, and I was able to swim with them, which was one of the most out-of-body, exhilarating experiences I’ve ever had. There was even a brief moment when I thought I was about to be kicked and/or swallowed by a whale, which was terrifyingly thrilling (don’t worry — I’m still here).

Even though a few of the days had rough seas and low visibility, I was able to swim with orcas later on during the trip, and I’ll never forget it.

After taking nearly a dozen safaris over the years, I was ready for something different. I’ve done the bigger camps and seen the Big 5, so I wanted to try a more niche wildlife experience.

I stayed at Tswalu’s Loapi Lodge in a two-bedroom villa, complete with a plunge pool and my own private chef. I much prefer a lodge to a tented camp, as hearing lions outside your tent at night and having no running water can be a lot to handle, and I’m done roughing it.

Unlike many safari destinations, Tswalu is unique because there aren’t any elephants, but you can see meerkat colonies and observe them relatively up close. I also spotted many black and white rhinos and cheetahs.

I highly recommend Tswalu to experienced safari-goers, but if it’s your first time, I’d suggest going to Cheetah Plains in Sabi Sands or Royal Malewane in Kruger National Park. You’ll get to see the Big 5 and have the perfect introduction to a safari (and you might get addicted to safaris, like I am!).

Many people skip the Caribbean in summer, but honestly, European summer heat can feel even more brutal, with beaches packed umbrella-to-umbrella in places like Spain, Italy and Portugal. This year, I canceled my summer trip to Portugal after a massive heat wave alert and went to Grand Cayman with my kids instead.

Yes, it was warm, but it didn’t feel any hotter than Europe would have (or even a humid Midwest or East Coast summer), and the beach was uncrowded and uncomplicated — no stairs or rugged terrain, like I’ve had to traverse in Portugal. Plus, no jet lag!

My stay at Palm Heights was peaceful, and even though it's a boutique hotel, it felt very family-friendly. I loved that my suite overlooked the white sands of Seven Mile Beach, and the spa was absolutely gorgeous. I highly recommend it for families, couples, or any type of traveler.

In my opinion, the Ritz Paris represents true luxury. I used Chase Points Boost to book it, getting more than 2 cents per point.

The hotel is unapologetically over-the-top, with gorgeous rooms and lavish decor, but what I really love are the service and amenities. The hotel has a program that lets you check in early in the morning after landing from a transatlantic flight, and consumer-friendly options like this are what make it feel truly luxurious. After all, true luxury goes beyond a beautiful room or view — hotels should solve problems, reduce friction, and make traveling easier.

Did you have any special hotel stays or travel experiences this year? Feel free to drop me a comment below and share yours, and be sure to check out our full list for Where to Go in 2027.

#6074. Senate Dems dismiss talk of earlier leadership election; Schumer confident

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a new majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec. 1.

That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.

The prospect of an earlier vote had been floated as a way to prevent internal divisions from hobbling the incoming majority before the 120th Congress even began.

But supporters of Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., both in the chamber and among party activists outside it, were increasingly casting the idea of a shorter contest as a bid to halt momentum for his bid against Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

Even as Schumer maintained that he has the votes necessary to be elected as majority leader, several senators insisted Tuesday the discussion taking place within the caucus was a good thing.

“I’m confident I’ll be the next leader. I have the votes,” Schumer told reporters on Tuesday following the conference’s lunch.

Van Hollen for his part told reporters Tuesday he believes his bid has “momentum at this point in time, which is why there was an effort to short-circuit the process.”

“And fortunately, I think that will fail.”

Several senators leaving the meeting said the topic of the leadership contest did not come up at all, and that neither Van Hollen nor Schumer gave a presentation regarding their bids.

That was in large part due to the absence of the incoming senators — which could be as high as 13, depending on how the dust settles in Alaska — who are able to vote in the leadership elections. Retiring senators do not cast a ballot.

With such a large class of incoming freshman, several incumbents saw it crucial to keep the election scheduled as is.

“No one has ever raised that with me. I mean, I saw a rumor that some were wanting to contemplate that,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Tuesday after the meeting. “The leadership discussions did not come up today. And part of the reason is we didn’t have the newcomers.”

“Remember, they all get a vote in the leadership discussion, and it would be hard to get them here,” Kaine continued, noting that only Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., was present for Tuesday’s lunch amid his belated orientation. “But nobody else was here, and that discussion needs to have the newcomers because newcomers get votes. The outgoers don’t, right?”

Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. echoed that sentiment on Monday evening, saying, “I want to hear from the freshman class as well.”

Sen. Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said, “I don’t know that” when asked about moving up the elections. “I think that we need to make sure that there’s enough time for what I would call a robust discussion about what we’re going to do. I think we should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here, and I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard.

“They’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table,” she said.

Several senators-elect are among those who have publicly thrown their hats into Van Hollen’s corner, including Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.El-Sayed on Tuesday said at The Atlantic Summit that he sees Van Hollen as “unique” in his experience in the Senate and running the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as well as what he called “a willingness to take risks.”

“We need people who are willing to take legislative risk,” he said. “We need to rethink the way we legislate. It just should not be the process where you make one or two omnibus pieces of legislation that nobody really knows what’s in them,” he continued, advocating for piecemeal legislation.

But there are about 15 Democrats who have publicly backed Schumer’s bid. If former Rep. Mary Peltola maintains her lead in the lone outstanding Senate race in Alaska, Schumer would need 29 to secure the helm of the ship.

“I committed to Sen. Schumer literally months ago, and I continue to support him,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said Monday. “I’m incredibly excited about the new ideas that our new colleagues have, and their energy, and the potential for changing the way we operate in the Senate, which we have to do because we need to be more effective.”

Several incumbents have also thrown their support behind Van Hollen for leadership change, including Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.“I think, as I’ve said many times, the American people want change in the way we do business here in Washington, and I think Chris Van Hollen would be a great leader of the Democrats,” Sanders said Monday.

Several senators and senators-elect are refusing to comment publicly on who they’ll back.

That included Sen. Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., who said he wants “to hear the commitments from folks that are pursuing this leadership role as well as every leadership position in the Senate, as well as chairs of committees, to what their commitments are to having a strong agenda that’s going to improve people’s lives.”

Kaine is also in that camp, and insisted Monday he hadn’t made up his mind. But he did speak positively of Schumer’s recruiting efforts in the midterms and history of dealing with a Trump White House.

“Schumer just delivered a major win for us. No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer,” he said. “Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in the caucus, and dealing with this wounded president is going to be a challenge over the next few years.”

“The voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change,” he said. “So we got to figure that out as a caucus, and we’re going to be able to. And we’re not afraid to have a discussion because we’re Democrats. We like democracy.”

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., also remained mum on who he’ll support but said, “You can’t argue” Schumer brought Democrats the majority.

“I think it’s a healthy thing to try and improve how the conference goes about its business,” he said. “I don’t think that is a distraction. We can deal with some distractions. We have to keep our eye on the ball.”

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who last week called for new leadership in a news conference with Sanders, days before Van Hollen’s announcement, was noncommittal arriving to the Capitol on Monday if that meant she’d be supporting the Maryland Democrat.

Senate Democrats’ election will most likely be a secret ballot. And most senators remained unified against moving the leadership elections before they recess for the Thanksgiving break.

“They should not be moved up. There was a reason that those rule changes took place before, and they should take place in December,” Lujan said.

Kaine dismissed Van Hollen’s challenge as anything unusual.

“We’re Democrats. It’s frankly unusual that there usually [aren’t] challenges to Democratic leaders because we’re Democrats,” he said. “It’s been a little unusual to have been here for 13 years and not really have them like this. But I think it’s a discussion not just about the two contenders for the leader role, but also the leadership team and priorities, and it’s all wrapped up in one discussion.”

“That’s why we decided, don’t do these votes until December, because you want to let the election settle and understand exactly what’s up, and then hear from potential votes.”

Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said, “I think we should stick with the rules when it comes to the caucus. … That’s going to be what makes sure that we show that we have a real process.”

Sanders asked: “Why would anyone want to do that?” when asked.

“I think there’s a date that’s been called, and that should be the date.”

#6073. Fake Amex Black Cards For $1,000—People Are Buying Status, But They May Be Committing A Crime

A man apparently made a fortune selling fake American Express Black Cards for about $1,000 apiece. The cards used buyers’ real account numbers, so when they paid for items the charges went onto their own bills. They were buying the appearance of being a Centurion cardmember. That’s the story told in this viral clip from Inside True Crime. His claim that customers could simply flash the cards to get into airport lounges is a lot harder to square with reality. View this post on Instagram

That’s the story told in this viral clip from Inside True Crime. His claim that customers could simply flash the cards to get into airport lounges is a lot harder to square with reality.

A post shared by Matthew Cox | Inside True Crime (@insidetruecrime)

Cox says the man put customers’ existing American Express numbers onto cards that looked like Centurion cards. They could pay for things, impress a date, and supposedly get waved into exclusive spaces. He says the business went on for years.

The comments split between people asking what the crime was, people asking where to order one, and frequent travelers pointing out that lounge access isn’t granted based on the look of the card – they run it through their system.

I’ve covered this sort of thing for years. Back in 2015, I wrote about a company that would turn an existing credit card into a custom metal card. Prices started at $99, with custom designs at $149 and gold plating at $249. That service couldn’t handle payment chips at the time. The payment system charges the account identified by the card’s credentials. Changing the material or artwork doesn’t change the rewards, spending power, or benefits attached to that account. And American Express itself has experimented with the physical form. In 2021, I covered artist-designed Centurion cards and a Prada wearable. Those were options Amex provided to real Centurion members. The Airport Lounge Claim Isn’t Plausible The reel makes a weird claim. It says the black card “doesn’t work,” then says it can pay for things. In the longer discussion, he means it doesn’t acquire the spending power he associates with a real Black Card. More importantly, Centurion Lounge access belongs to eligible cardmembers. A Gold account dressed up as Centurion is still a Gold account when its eligibility is checked. It hasn’t acquired lounge access, Centurion access priority, or any other benefit. Paying Your Own Bill Doesn’t Make It Legal The comments ask “what’s the crime?” Using someone else’s account to steal money is different from paying your own restaurant bill with a customized card. But there are several separate issues here. The maker copying Amex branding. Selling a replica with American Express branding raises trademark infringement issues. The concern is whether it falsely appears to be an Amex-issued or approved product. Depending on the marks and conduct, criminal trademark counterfeiting can also apply. The customer paying normally. An altered card isn’t automatically federal credit card fraud. The federal access-device statute includes altered and counterfeit cards, but requires intent to defraud. Merely wanting a date to think you’re rich isn’t enough. The customer claiming benefits they haven’t earned. Passing off the card as proof of Centurion membership to obtain restricted lounge services, a waived fee, or another benefit creates a different problem. It’s not obvious this would even work. And paying the bar tab doesn’t pay for the separate service obtained through deception. Using the fake credential to support false claims in a credit transaction would be a separate problem. Several state laws could be implicated. Texas has separate credit card, forgery, and counterfeit card rules. And Amex’s October 2023 U.S. merchant regulations instructed merchants not to accept a card that appeared physically altered. Getting a transaction approved doesn’t prove the replacement card was authorized, even if the merchant doesn’t know. Banks spend money on cards that look and feel good. Paying $1,000 to pretend you have a different one is an expensive way to impress someone who’s watching you pay. That’s more than the $895 first year’s annual fee on an actual Platinum Card, which comes with actual Centurion Lounge access. The card just wouldn’t be black. #6072. Trump country cracked: 5 races that saw double-digit Trump territory fall to Democrats in 2026

Senator John Fetterman joins 'Saturday in America' for his first interview since the midterms. Fetterman discusses the rise of far-left candidates in the Democratic Party, potential investigations and facing primary challenges.

Donald Trump carried Mississippi by nearly 23 points in 2024. Two years later, Democrat Scott Colom won the state’s Senate race, ending a Republican hold that had lasted more than four decades.

Colom’s victory was part of a string of Democratic breakthroughs during the midterms in places Trump had carried by double digits. Democrats also won Senate races in Kansas and South Carolina, captured the Texas governor’s office and flipped a Republican-held House seat deep in Trump country in Indiana that had not elected a Democrat since 1990.

The results stand out for more than the presidential margins as well — Democrats broke Senate streaks that had lasted decades and defeated Republican incumbents in races many expected the GOP to hold, including one where the Democratic challenger spent next to nothing on television advertisements.

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE

Here are five of the year’s most striking upsets:

Democratic and Republican Party emblems are displayed with an American flag background in this photo illustration taken on Aug. 25, 2022. Democrats flipped several red-state seats during the 2026 midterm elections. (Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Trump carried the state by nearly 23 points in 2024, and a Democrat had not won a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi since 1982. Several major election forecasters rated the contest Solid Republican for much of the cycle, before shifting it to Likely Republican as the race tightened.

Colom, a district attorney, defeated Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., by less than one percentage point, 49.36% to 48.54%, according to Associated Press election results. Hyde-Smith had Trump’s backing, and the president rallied for her in the campaign’s final days. Meanwhile, the Senate Leadership Fund, a super PAC aligned with Senate GOP leadership, made a seven-figure late-campaign ad buy, as previously reported by Fox News Digital.

The Associated Press did not call the race until Nov. 11, more than a week after Election Day. Colom will also become the first Black senator to represent Mississippi since Reconstruction.

The margin was razor-thin, but the political barrier was enormous — a Trump +23 state, a Trump-backed incumbent and a 44-year drought in Democratic Senate victories. But Democrats pulled off the upset.

Scott Colom walks across the campus of Jackson State University on Election Day, Nov. 3, 2026, in Jackson, Miss. Colom defeated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, ending a 44-year Democratic Senate drought in the state. (Aron Smith/Jackson State University via Getty Images)

Hinojosa, a Democratic state representative, defeated three-term Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, R-Texas, as he sought an unprecedented fourth term, ending a 36-year Democratic losing streak in Texas governor’s races. Trump had carried the state by 13.7 points in 2024, according to Associated Press election data, and an October Fox News poll showed Abbott ahead leading up to the Nov. 3 election. Hinojosa, however, ultimately won with 52.8% of the vote to Abbott’s 45.7%, according to Associated Press election results.

Her victory was a major break from Texas’ recent political history and a miss by many major polls. It also made Hinojosa the state’s first Latina governor. Democrats had not won the governor’s office since Ann Richards’ 1990 victory.

Texas state Rep. Gina Hinojosa speaks during a campaign rally in Austin on Nov. 2, 2026. She unseated GOP Gov. Greg Abbott. (Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Hinojosa’s win was one of two Democratic statewide breakthroughs in Texas, as Democratic state Rep. James Talarico also defeated Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Senate race.

CHUCK DEVORE: TEXAS TURNS BLUE, BUT HERE’S WHERE THE NEXT 4 BIG BATTLES ARE COMING

South Carolina had not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1998, when Fritz Hollings won his final term, and Trump carried the state by nearly 18 points in 2024, according to Associated Press election data. Andrews, a Democratic pediatrician who had never held elected office before, defeated appointed Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, by nearly five points.

Graham had Trump’s endorsement and the president also helped her with late campaign appearances on the trail. She had been appointed to serve out her brother’s term after his death, then won the Republican nomination for a full six-year term.

Andrews’ win broke a nearly three-decade Republican hold on the state’s Senate seat and became a rare moment when a Trump-backed candidate lost in a state Republicans had long counted on.

Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews face off during a South Carolina U.S. Senate debate in Columbia on Oct. 11, 2026. Andrews went on to defeat Graham, ending a nearly three-decade Republican hold on the seat. (Courtesy: SCETV)

Kansas had not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932, when George McGill won a full term. Hamilton, a Democrat and the founding pastor of a large United Methodist church, defeated first-term Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., in a state Trump carried by 16 points in 2024, according to election data from the Associated Press.

The Kansas race was long viewed as a Republican hold, but major election forecasters moved it into toss-up territory late in the campaign as Marshall faced scrutiny over his residency and lawsuits his former medical practice filed against patients.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance both campaigned for Marshall, and Republican-aligned groups spent heavily to keep the seat, including more than $26 million committed to ads supporting him after the August primary — more than was spent on Marshall during his first race in 2020, according to AdImpact data cited by the Associated Press.

Hamilton’s win ended a 94-year Republican Senate streak.

Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., left, and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton, who became the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from Kansas since 1932. (Getty Images)

Democrat J.D. Ford defeated three-term Rep. Victoria Spartz, R-Ind., in Indiana’s 5th Congressional District, which Trump carried by about 17 points, according to Associated Press election results from 2024. Spartz had won re-election there by 18.6 points in 2024, and the district had not elected a Democrat since 1990, when Jim Jontz won.

Ford, a Democratic state senator, won 51.7% to Spartz’s 48.3%, according to the Associated Press results after the midterms. His victory was the only Indiana House seat to change parties, making it a sharp reversal in a state that Trump carried by 19 points statewide in 2024.

The U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on June 25, 2025. Democrats scored several upsets in double-digit Trump states and districts during the 2026 midterm elections. (Eric Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Democrats also flipped several other Republican-held House seats in districts Trump carried by double digits, including in North Carolina. Democrat Richard Ojeda defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, R-N.C., who chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee, the House GOP’s campaign and fundraising arm. Hudson was charged with helping protect the Republican majority, and he had raised $4.2 million to Ojeda’s $2.9 million and won the district by nearly 19 points in 2024, while Trump had carried it by 16 points.

In North Carolina’s 6th District, Democrat Cyril Jefferson defeated first-term Rep. Addison McDowell, R-N.C., in a district Trump carried by nearly 17 points, and Democrat Zach Dembo also flipped an open, Republican-held seat in Kentucky’s 6th District, beating Republican Ralph Alvarado by 9.4 points in a district Trump had carried by roughly 15 points in 2024.

Meanwhile, a razor-thin margin in Tennessee’s 4th District underscores the challenges Republicans faced across several traditionally safe districts. Democrat Victoria Broderick, who spent under $100,000 and had no record of airing any paid TV ads, leads incumbent Rep. Scott DesJarlais, R-Tenn., by 277 votes in the latest count, and DesJarlais conceded the race on Nov. 16. Fox News Digital previously reported that Broderick spent under $100,000 compared to DesJarlais’ more than $500,000. The Associated Press has yet to formally call the race with 99% of the vote counted so far.

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.
